---
title: "StatTables"
title-block-banner: false
page-layout: full
toc: false
---

Interactive versions of the statistical tables used in introductory statistics. Instead of reading a printed table, enter a value to get the area under the curve, or enter an area to get the critical value, in one or both tails. Each table opens on its own page.

```{=html}
<div class="app-grid">
  <a class="app-card" href="z_table.html">
    <i class="bi bi-table"></i>
    <h3>Z-Table</h3>
    <p>Standard normal distribution, Z ~ N(0, 1): areas for a z-score, or the z-score for a chosen area.</p>
    <span>Open table →</span>
  </a>
  <a class="app-card" href="t_table.html">
    <i class="bi bi-table"></i>
    <h3>T-Table</h3>
    <p>Student's t distribution with df = n − 1: areas for a t-score, or the critical value t*.</p>
    <span>Open table →</span>
  </a>
  <a class="app-card" href="chi_square_table.html">
    <i class="bi bi-table"></i>
    <h3>Chi-Square Table</h3>
    <p>Right-skewed χ² distribution: areas and the left and right critical values, which are not symmetric.</p>
    <span>Open table →</span>
  </a>
  <a class="app-card" href="f_table.html">
    <i class="bi bi-table"></i>
    <h3>F-Table</h3>
    <p>F distribution with two degrees of freedom, used to compare variances and in ANOVA.</p>
    <span>Open table →</span>
  </a>
  <a class="app-card" href="tukey_table.html">
    <i class="bi bi-table"></i>
    <h3>Tukey q-Table</h3>
    <p>Studentized range distribution Q(k, df): critical values and p-values for comparing k means after ANOVA.</p>
    <span>Open table →</span>
  </a>
</div>
```
